hints: Notice the thick wire and thin wire are in series with the cell, so ask what must be identical at every point in a series loop.
Recall $I = nAvq$ for a metal wire, where $A$ is cross-sectional area and $v$ is electron drift speed, and both wires are copper.
Compare the areas: with $I$ and $n$ fixed, decide whether the electrons in the larger-area thick wire need to drift faster or slower to carry the same current.
walkthrough: Identify the circuit condition: the thick wire and thin wire are in series, so the current $I$ is the same in both wires.
State the governing relation for conduction: $I = nAvq$, where $n$ is number density of free electrons, $A$ is cross-sectional area, $v$ is mean drift speed and $q$ is electron charge.
Use the material information: both wires are copper, so $n$ and $q$ are the same in the two wires, and $I$ is the same from step 1.
Rearrange to $v = I/(nAq)$: for fixed $I$, $n$ and $q$, drift speed is inversely proportional to area $A$.
Apply the area comparison: the thick wire has significantly larger $A$ than the thin wire, so its $v$ must be significantly smaller to give the same $I$.

options.A: In series the current is the same everywhere, so charge per unit time $I = Q/t$ is the same in the thick and thin wire.
options.B: From $I = nAvq$ with same $I$ and same $n$ for copper, larger area $A$ in the thick wire requires smaller drift speed $v$.
options.C: Both wires are copper, so the number of free electrons per unit volume $n$ is a material property and is the same.
options.D: Same current means same charge per second, so the number of electrons passing per second $I/e$ is also the same.
